text: {"rules":[{"jurisdiction":"Berkeley, CA","level":"city","category":"algorithmic_rent_setting","status":"in_force","title":"Prohibition on the sale or use of coordinated pricing algorithms to set rents or manage occupancy levels (BMC Chapter 13.63)","requirement":"It is unlawful to sell, license, or otherwise provide to Berkeley landlords any coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in Berkeley. It is also unlawful for a landlord to use such an algorithm when setting rents or occupancy levels. A coordinated pricing algorithm is a computation process that uses non-public Competitor Data (less than 90 days old) to recommend rents, fees, occupancy rates or other lease terms in coordination between a Berkeley landlord and its competitors, including through a third-party vendor. The chapter does not cap rents. Each month a violation continues and each unit for which the algorithm was used is a separate violation. The City Attorney may sue for damages, injunctive relief, restitution and civil penalties.
